उषा १

UṢĀ I . The daughter of Bāṇāsura and the wife of aniruddha.1) Genealogy. Descended from viṣṇu in the following order:-brahmā-kaśyapa-hiraṇyakaśipu-PrahlādaVirocana-mahābali-bāṇa-uṣā.
2) marriage of uṣā. See under aniruddha.

उषा २

UṢĀ II . The daughter of a hermit. The king of Śālva once attacked satyaratha, the king of vidarbha, and killed him. The queens of the king of vidarbha went to the forest. One of them who was pregnant gave birth to a child on the bank of a river. When she got down into the river to drink water, a crocodile swallowed her. Then a hermit's daughter named uṣā brought up the child. (śiva purāṇa).

उषा ३

UṢĀ III . The night is called uṣā and the day, Ghuṣṭi. The time between uṣā and Ghuṣṭi is called sandhyā. (viṣṇu purāṇa, Aṁ a 2, Chapter 8).

उषंगु १

UṢAṄGU I . A hermit who lived in the western country. (M.B. śānti Parva, Chapter 208, Stanza 30).

उषंगु २

UṢAṄGU II . A synonym of śiva. (M.B. anuśāsana parva, Chapter 17, Stanza 105).

उषंगु ३

UṢAṄGU III . A king of the yadu family. His father was vṛjinīvān and his son was called citraratha. (M.B. anu āsana Parva, Chapter 147, Stanza 29).

उशंगव

UŚAṄGAVA . A member of the durbar of the king yama (god of death). (M.B. Sabhā Parva, Chapter 8, Stanza 26).

उशंकु

UŚAṄKU (ruśaṅku) . A hermit. Seeing that old age was coming on him this hermit forsook his body in the pṛthūdaka tīrtha and went to the realm of viṣṇu. ārṣṭiṣeṇa, viśvāmitra, sindhudvīpa, devāpi and such others got Brāhmaṇya (the state of being Brahmin) by doing penance in the hermitage of this hermit. (M.B. śānti Parva, Chapter 38, Stanzas 33-39).

उशनस्

UŚANAS . The teacher śukra, the son of the hermit Bhrgu. (See under śukra).
